title: JS: TypeScript, Node and React (topics 15-20)
_note: rv2 S2 (PLAN §2.2 fund-js-platform row). Scope = Fundamentals JS topic gates 15-20. Sources = the topic gate plus its first drill; siblings = the bug-hunt drill and related.json drills. Server-local side file, never stamped.

ideas.idea: Type data from outside the program as unknown and narrow it with checks (typeof, in, a discriminant field) before use; any switches the checker off.
ideas.why: An any-typed payload compiles everywhere and fails at runtime, far from the place where the bad data entered.
ideas.prompt: A webhook handler does `const event = JSON.parse(body) as any` and reads event.data.amount. A malformed event crashes a nightly job three services away. How should the handler be typed?
ideas.answer: Parse into unknown and prove its shape before use: check it is an object, check the discriminating type field, check that amount is a number, then treat it as the narrowed union member. Reject anything else at the edge with a clear error. The compiler then guarantees that later code only sees validated events.

ideas.idea: A generic type parameter expresses a relation between inputs and outputs, such as 'returns the same type it was given'; without a relation it is just a disguised any.
ideas.why: Functions typed with wide unions or any lose the link between argument and result, so every caller casts and the checker stops catching mismatches.
ideas.prompt: `function pick(obj: object, keys: string[]): object` forces every caller to cast its result. Rewrite the signature so the result type follows the arguments, and say what the generics guarantee.
ideas.answer: `function pick<T, K extends keyof T>(obj: T, keys: K[]): Pick<T, K>`. T captures the input's type, K is limited to its real keys, and the result is exactly those properties. A typo in a key becomes a compile error, and callers get a precise type with no cast.

ideas.idea: Streams move data in chunks with backpressure: when the writer is full, the reader must pause; pipeline() wires that up and propagates errors and cleanup.
ideas.why: Reading faster than you can write buffers the whole input in memory, and hand-wired pipes leak file handles when one side fails.
ideas.prompt: A Node script copies a 10 GB export to a slow network share with `readable.on('data', c => writable.write(c))`. Memory climbs until the process dies. What is wrong, and what do you write instead?
ideas.answer: write() returns false when the destination's buffer is full, but the handler ignores it and keeps reading, so chunks pile up in memory. Use stream.pipeline(readable, writable) from node:stream/promises: it pauses the reader until the writer drains, and if either side errors it destroys both and rejects.

ideas.idea: Validate requests at the HTTP edge and pick the status by who must act: the client's mistake is a 4xx with a reason, the server's own failure is a 5xx.
ideas.why: Unvalidated input fails deep inside the code as a 500, and wrong status codes make clients retry what can never succeed or give up on what would.
ideas.prompt: POST /orders with a missing quantity currently crashes inside the pricing code and returns 500. Clients retry it in a loop. What should the endpoint do?
ideas.answer: Check the body at the route before any work: a missing or invalid field is the client's to fix, so answer 400 (or 422) with which field and why, and clients stop retrying. A 500 is only for failures on the server's side, which a retry might cure. Map not found, conflict and auth errors to their own statuses too.

ideas.idea: React state is a snapshot for one render: setting it schedules a new render, render must be pure, and updates replace objects instead of mutating them.
ideas.why: Mutating state in place or reading it right after setState shows stale values and skipped re-renders, bugs that look random.
ideas.prompt: A click handler calls `setCount(count + 1)` three times and the counter only goes up by one. Another handler does `cart.items.push(item); setCart(cart)` and nothing re-renders. Explain both.
ideas.answer: In one render count is a fixed snapshot, so all three calls set the same value; use the updater form setCount(c => c + 1) to build on the latest value. The push mutates the existing object and passes the same reference back, so React sees no change; create a new object and a new items array instead.

ideas.idea: An effect keeps a component in sync with something outside React; list every value it reads as a dependency and return a cleanup that undoes it.
ideas.why: Missing dependencies leave stale closures that act on old props, and missing cleanup leaves subscriptions, timers and late fetches writing into unmounted or changed screens.
ideas.prompt: A profile page fetches `/users/${id}` in an effect with an empty dependency array. Switching quickly between users sometimes shows the wrong person. Fix the effect and explain why it broke.
ideas.answer: The effect reads id but never re-runs when it changes, and nothing stops an older, slower response from landing last. Put id in the dependency array and return a cleanup that aborts the request (AbortController) or ignores its result, so only the latest user's response updates state.
